themes.name: Successful release delivery
themes.summary: The team reported strong collaboration during release week and delivered the milestone on the planned date.

themes.name: Late-cycle quality gaps
themes.summary: A recurring concern is that many bugs reached QA late in the sprint; feedback also points toward earlier QA alignment on test scope before formal testing.

themes.name: Process discipline (ceremonies and reviews)
themes.summary: Daily syncs frequently ran over schedule, and the team raised ideas to tighten pull-request review before merge.

strengths.summary: The team noted strong collaboration during release week.
The team delivered the milestone on the planned date.

concerns.summary: A large number of bugs escaped to QA late in the sprint.
Daily sync meetings often ran over the scheduled time.

opportunities.summary: The team sees value in aligning with QA on test scope before formal testing starts.
The team suggested that pull requests require two reviewers before merge.

suggestedActions.title: Add mid-sprint dev–QA test-scope sync
suggestedActions.reason: FB-0005 shows QA scope misalignment late in the cycle; FB-0003 shows bugs reaching QA too late. A fixed mid-sprint checkpoint lets QA confirm coverage and dev flag at-risk stories before the final handoff.

suggestedActions.title: Require two reviewers on every release-path PR
suggestedActions.reason: FB-0006 calls for two reviewers on PRs. Making dual review mandatory on main and release branches spreads review load and catches issues before late-cycle QA churn.

suggestedActions.title: Timebox daily standups to 15 minutes
suggestedActions.reason: FB-0004 reports dailies running too long. A 15-minute cap with a parking-lot channel for deep dives keeps ceremony discipline without losing blocker visibility.

suggestedActions.title: Introduce a pre-QA merge checklist
suggestedActions.reason: FB-0003 highlights late bugs handed to QA. A short checklist before the QA queue reduces rework at the end of the sprint.

suggestedActions.title: Align acceptance criteria with QA during sprint planning
suggestedActions.reason: FB-0005 flags test-scope gaps. Reviewing acceptance criteria with QA when stories are committed keeps expected coverage explicit from day one.

suggestedActions.title: Document what worked in the recent release
suggestedActions.reason: FB-0001 and FB-0002 credit successful release delivery. Capturing the practices that worked gives the team a repeatable playbook for the next cycle.

limitations: Human review is required before any suggested action is approved.
Analysis identifies process patterns, not individuals.
Observations are not proof of causality.
Six anonymous items may not represent the full team experience for Sprint 1.
